A0055.title: Vulnerability Identification
A0055.definition: The process of detecting and identifying potential security vulnerabilities in computer systems, networks, or applications.
A0055.description: Vulnerability identification detects systems, networks, or applications through scanners, manual reviews, and vulnerability intelligence comparison, employing rule matching, version comparison, and baseline verification to identify known vulnerabilities, configuration errors, and logic flaws. It typically includes automated scanning, manual code review, vulnerability database matching, and system/application/configuration vulnerability identification.
A0055.limitation: Vulnerability identification faces several limitations. First, the incompleteness of vulnerability databases may leave certain vulnerabilities uncovered. Second, automated tools and scanners may produce false positives—incorrectly flagging non-existent vulnerabilities—while also missing real vulnerabilities, resulting in false negatives. Furthermore, for complex applications and custom-developed systems, relying solely on automated tools may fail to discover all vulnerabilities comprehensively, and manual review incurs high costs. Therefore, vulnerability identification requires a combination of approaches, including automated tools, manual review, continuous vulnerability database updates, and regular system audits, to improve comprehensiveness and accuracy.

references.title: NIST SP 800-40 Rev. 4: Guide to Enterprise Patch Management Planning
